feature.name: secret-self-service
feature.summary: SOPS-based GitOps self-service secret management: developers list and submit Key Vault secrets for an app/environment/target (live=infrastructure-live, sand=service-catalog) via a new Vue page and two backend endpoints. An app/environment may resolve to one or more Key Vault directories, discovered by enumerating the target repo's tree once (not path-probing) over BOTH accepted roots (infrastructure/ and azureDatabricks/) and disambiguated by vaultDir when more than one is found; sub-apps under a grouping directory (e.g. idm/_idmapplications/<subapp>) are disambiguated by an optional qualifier. Values are SOPS-encrypted (wrapKey-only) and committed via PR; the portal never decrypts or displays values, and post-merge CI sync is out of scope for portal tracking.

user_stories.i_want: to see the list of existing secret names for my app/environment without leaving the portal
user_stories.so_that: I know what already exists before creating a new one

user_stories.i_want: to submit a new or updated secret value through a form
user_stories.so_that: I never need Azure Portal access or a manual platform ticket

user_stories.i_want: to choose whether I'm working against live (infrastructure-live) or sand (service-catalog) infrastructure
user_stories.so_that: the secret lands in the correct repository/environment scope

user_stories.i_want: every secret submission to open an auditable PR with correlationId and submitter email
user_stories.so_that: I can review and approve before it reaches Key Vault

user_stories.i_want: assurance that the portal backend only ever holds wrapKey (encrypt-only) access
user_stories.so_that: a portal compromise can never decrypt existing secrets

user_stories.as: an application developer whose app owns more than one Key Vault (e.g. mlops-style keyvault01/keyvault02)
user_stories.i_want: to be shown all resolved vaults and asked to pick one before I submit or filter a secret
user_stories.so_that: my secret lands in the vault I intend, not whichever one a fallback happened to pick

criteria: GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment?target=live|sand[&vaultDir=...][&qualifier=...] returns { success, data: [{ name, vaultDir, vaultName, lastUpdated }], correlationId }
requireAuth applied; unauthenticated -> 401

appName validated /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ (widened from /^[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,8}$/ to accept real-tree values like azureDatabricks, ayaApplications, facilityContracts); target validated against ['live','sand']; environment validated /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$/ (widened from /^[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,16}$/ to accept hyphenated real-tree values like shared-services); environment is existence-checked via FR-003 (not against data/environments.json)

Optional qualifier query param, validated /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, disambiguates sub-apps under a parent appName (e.g. idm with qualifier=notif narrows to infrastructure/idm/_idmapplications/notif/...). When supplied, it must match a discovered FR-003 sub-app for (appName, environment) under the same target; mismatch -> 422. When omitted, FR-003 must resolve at most one sub-app for (appName, environment); ambiguity (e.g. idm with no qualifier and multiple idm/notif+idm/autobk etc.) -> 422 with the qualifier list returned so the client can render a sub-app selector
Response never includes value/plaintext fields
Secret names read from the plaintext YAML keys of secrets.enc.yaml, sibling to each resolved vault directory ({vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml); no Azure Key Vault SDK call
FR-003 found=false, or no secrets.enc.yaml exists in any resolved vault directory -> 404 { success:false, error, correlationId }

When FR-003 resolves more than one vault, the response aggregates secrets across all of them, each entry tagged with its source vaultDir; the same secret name may legitimately appear in two sibling vaults and both are listed, never deduped
Optional vaultDir query param filters the response to a single vault; if supplied it must exactly match one of the FR-003 vaultDir values, otherwise -> 422
correlationId present in every response and log line
p95 latency <= 2000ms (NFR-PERF-001)

POST /api/secrets accepts { target, appName, environment, vaultDir, qualifier, secretName, secretValue, correlationId }; vaultDir is optional when FR-003 resolves exactly one vault, required when it resolves more than one; qualifier is optional when FR-003 resolves exactly one sub-app for (appName, environment), required when it resolves more than one
express-validator validates target enum, appName /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, environment /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$/, qualifier (when supplied) /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, secretName /^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,127}$/
secretValue is never logged; only { secretName, appName, environment, qualifier (if supplied), correlationId } logged
Value is SOPS-encrypted (wrapKey) before any persistence; raw value never written to disk/Git/log

vaultDir is allow-list validated for membership in the current FR-003 discovery result for (appName, environment, qualifier) BEFORE any path construction (regex validation alone is insufficient — an unvalidated vaultDir is an arbitrary-repo-path write)

qualifier is allow-list validated for membership in the current FR-003 sub-app list for (appName, environment) under the same target; mismatch -> 422 with the qualifier list returned so the client can render a sub-app selector

Encrypted doc committed to the selected target repo at {vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml, derived from vaultDir directly (never reconstructed from vaultName or app/env/qualifier) — one document per vault, never merged across sibling vaults
PR opened against target repo default branch; description includes target, appName, environment, qualifier (if supplied), secretName, correlationId, req.user.email
Success response is { success:true, correlationId, prNumber, prUrl }

Branch name is deterministic: secrets/{appName}-{environment}-{qualifier?qualifier+'-':''}{vaultSlug}-{secretName}, where vaultSlug is the final path segment of vaultDir (e.g. keyvault, keyvault01) — required so two sibling vaults submitting the same secret name never collide on one branch; existing open PR on that branch -> 409 { success:false, error, prUrl, correlationId }
Endpoint is synchronous end-to-end (encrypt+commit+PR in one request/response); no workflow dispatch, no useWorkflowPolling, no /api/status polling
FR-003 found:false -> 422; found:true + vaultName:null is NOT an error and proceeds normally, since the commit path derives from vaultDir, not vaultName
vaultDir omitted with >1 vaults resolved -> 422 { success:false, error, vaults, correlationId } (vaults is the FR-003 list, so the client can render a selector without a second call)
vaultDir supplied but not an exact match to one of the FR-003 vaultDir values -> 422

qualifier omitted with >1 sub-apps resolved for (appName, environment) -> 422 { success:false, error, qualifiers, correlationId } (qualifiers is the FR-003 sub-app list, so the client can render a sub-app selector)
qualifier supplied but not an exact match to one of the FR-003 sub-app values -> 422

Concurrency: compare the target repo's current default-branch secrets.enc.yaml content SHA (at the same vaultDir being written) to the SHA captured when this submission's branch was created/last based; mismatch -> abort, no merge attempt, 503 { success:false, error, correlationId }. Scoped to the single {vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml being written — a concurrent submission to a sibling vault of the same app/environment touches a different file and must not trigger this path
resolveKeyVaults(appName, environment, target, qualifier) reads the target repo via githubService.octokit (never codeOctokit)

Discovery is tree enumeration, not path probing: one GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{defaultBranchSha}?recursive=1 call, filtering entries under a root table whose keys are accepted top-level directories:
- infrastructure/ — whose paths are matched positionally-agnostically for appName/environment/qualifier/sub-app nesting
- azureDatabricks/ — whose paths are matched as <env>/keyvault with a synthetic appName='azureDatabricks' and no qualifier

A path qualifies when its FINAL path segment matches /^keyvault\d*$/i (directories) or keyvault.hcl under a non-shared environment directory; shared _common/common/shared keyvault.hcl files are Terragrunt include configs and are excluded from selectable vaults
For infrastructure/ paths: appName/environment/qualifier are derived positionally-agnostically from the matched path's segments (not assumed to occupy fixed depths). A path qualifies when:
- its first segment after infrastructure/ equals appName, AND
- any subsequent segment equals environment, AND
- any segment between appName and environment that is NOT environment and NOT in the grouping-dir skip-list (keyvaults, _idmapplications, etc.) is treated as a sub-app qualifier

This correctly handles depth-2 canonical layout, numbered vault dirs (keyvault01/keyvault02), depth-3 {app}/hub/{env}, {app}/{env}/{subapp} sub-app nesting, and {app}/{grouping}/{subapp}/{env} (e.g. idm/_idmapplications/notif/dev)
For azureDatabricks/ paths: the path is matched as azureDatabricks/<env>/keyvault with appName='azureDatabricks', environment=<env>, and no qualifier

The environment-agnostic shared heuristic is widened to /(^_?common$|^shared$)/i (from /_?common$/i) so that infrastructure/ayaApplications/ayaCoreServices/keyvaults/shared/keyvault is returned for any selected environment, not only when environment='shared'

The previously-specified fallback scan of *.hcl under infrastructure/{appName}/{environment}/ is WITHDRAWN — it is non-recursive and depth-2-anchored and rescues none of the real layout variants; it is not carried forward as a safety net

Returns { found: boolean, vaults: Array<{ vaultDir, vaultName, resourceGroup }>, qualifiers?: string[] }; found is true when at least one qualifying vault directory/file exists and is the authoritative existence check for FR-001/FR-002; vaultDir is always populated when found=true; vaultName/resourceGroup are best-effort and may be null even when found=true; found=false -> vaults is an empty array. qualifiers is present and non-empty when more than one sub-app resolves for (appName, environment) under the same target, listing the distinct qualifier values so the client can render a sub-app selector. Callers must never assume vaults.length === 1

Name reconstruction (vaultName) is delegated to the new services/terragruntLocalsResolver.js — it follows local.{alias}.locals.keyvaultname indirection into env.hcl/common.hcl under a varying alias (env, config, common_vars), evaluates substr()/format()/interpolation over the small observed expression grammar, and strips full-line comments before matching so a commented-out '# keyvaultname = ...' line is never matched as live. Reuses the same githubService.octokit client and GitHub App auth as hclParser.js — this is NOT a reuse of hclParser.js's parsing capability, which only extracts module{}.source/version from a single file and has zero cross-file locals resolution, expression evaluation, or comment stripping

Results are cached in-process for 5 minutes, keyed by target ALONE (repo-level) — one tree fetch serves every app/environment/vault lookup in that repo. The cache stores the in-flight Promise so concurrent callers across differing app/environment tuples share one underlying GitHub call (stampede protection)

If the trees API response returns truncated:true (GitHub truncates above ~100k entries/7MB), fall back to per-directory listing for the requested appName rather than silently returning found:false; log a warning with the correlation ID
Unconfigured target repo -> returns { found:false, vaults:[] } and logs a warning; does not throw
secrets nav entry added to srcV2/stores/navigation.ts PageId union and rendered in SharedHeader when authenticated
New page component srcV2/pages/SecretsPage.vue (Composition API, TypeScript)
Page renders target selector (live/sand) above app/environment/qualifier selector; changing target re-runs the list call
On mount calls GET /api/secrets/apps?target= to populate app/environment/qualifier selectors; on selection calls GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment?target=&qualifier=
Secrets list shows name, vaultName, lastUpdated only — never a value field

The secrets list also shows each secret's source vaultDir and offers a filter when more than one vault resolves, so identically-named secrets in sibling vaults stay distinguishable

When FR-003 resolves more than one sub-app for (appName, environment) (e.g. idm with multiple _idmapplications sub-apps), the form renders a required sub-app selector populated from the qualifiers list and submit stays disabled until a sub-app is chosen; when exactly one sub-app resolves, the selector is hidden and that sub-app is used implicitly
The app selector accepts appName values up to 64 chars (widened from 8) and environment values up to 32 chars (widened from 16), matching the new regexes
The app selector includes the synthetic appName='azureDatabricks' when target=live, exposing the azureDatabricks/<env>/keyvault paths as a single app

GET /api/environments passthrough unchanged, returns the new key automatically

Flipping secrets:true for one environment in JSON activates the page for that environment with no code change
Every secrets handler logs correlationId, user email, target, appName, environment on every code path
No log line in services/secretsService.js or the secrets route handlers uses a 'value' field key
PR descriptions include correlationId + user email, never the secret value
logMetric('secret_create_submitted', ...) and logMetric('secret_list_fetched', ...) follow the app_list_fetched structured pattern
All secrets endpoints require target in {'live','sand'}; any other value -> 400
live maps to config.github.infrastructureLiveRepo, sand maps to config.github.serviceRepo
Both use githubService.octokit (Infrastructure GitHub App) only — never codeOctokit
SecretsPage.vue renders the live/sand selector above app/environment selection; changing it re-runs discovery/list
target is included in every FR-006 log event and every FR-002 PR description
target determines the single repository written to per request; no cross-target writes

query.vaultDir?: string (optional, filters to a single vault)

api_endpoints.purpose: List secret names (no values) for an app/environment in the selected target repo, optionally filtered by sub-app qualifier or vaultDir

response_schema.data: { name: string, vaultDir: string, vaultName: string|null, lastUpdated: string }[]

errors.condition: FR-003 found=false or no secrets.enc.yaml in any resolved vault
vaultDir query param supplied but does not match any FR-003-resolved vaultDir; or qualifier supplied but does not match any FR-003-resolved sub-app

api_endpoints.purpose: SOPS-encrypt and commit a new/updated secret via PR to the selected target repo, optionally scoped to a sub-app qualifier

request_schema.qualifier: string (optional if exactly 1 sub-app resolves for (appName, environment); required if >1; must exactly match an FR-003-resolved sub-app)
request_schema.vaultDir: string (optional if exactly 1 vault resolves; required if >1; must exactly match an FR-003-resolved vaultDir)

errors.condition: FR-003 found=false; or >1 vaults resolved and vaultDir omitted (returns vaults list); or vaultDir supplied but not an allow-listed match; or >1 sub-apps resolved and qualifier omitted (returns qualifiers list); or qualifier supplied but not an allow-listed match
open PR already exists on the deterministic branch
concurrent write detected via file-SHA mismatch on the same vaultDir's secrets.enc.yaml

resolve_key_vaults_result.found: boolean — true when at least one qualifying vault directory/file exists; authoritative existence check for FR-001/FR-002
resolve_key_vaults_result.vaults: Array<{ vaultDir: string, vaultName: string|null, resourceGroup: string|null }> — empty when found=false; vaultDir always populated when found=true; vaultName/resourceGroup best-effort, may be null while found=true. Callers must never assume vaults.length === 1
resolve_key_vaults_result.qualifiers: string[] — present (possibly empty) when found=true; non-empty when more than one sub-app resolves for (appName, environment) under the same target, so the client can render a sub-app selector

secret_list_item.name: string
secret_list_item.vaultDir: string — repo-relative directory path of the source vault, e.g. infrastructure/mlops/dev/keyvault02
secret_list_item.lastUpdated: string (ISO 8601, from that vault's secrets.enc.yaml latest commit)

secrets_page_state.qualifiers: string[] | null — list of distinct sub-app qualifiers for (appName, environment) when >1; drives the sub-app selector when present
secrets_page_state.selectedQualifier: string | null — required before submit when qualifiers.length > 1; implicit when qualifiers.length === 1
secrets_page_state.vaults: Array<{ vaultDir, vaultName, resourceGroup }> — from the last FR-003 resolution; drives the vault selector when length > 1
secrets_page_state.selectedVaultDir: string | null — required before submit when vaults.length > 1; implicit when vaults.length === 1
secrets_page_state.submitResult: { prNumber: number, prUrl: string, correlationId: string } | null
secrets_page_state.submitError: { message: string, correlationId: string, vaults?: Array<{vaultDir,vaultName,resourceGroup}>, qualifiers?: string[] } | null

component_changes.description: resolveKeyVaults(appName, environment, target, qualifier?) — tree enumeration (see FR-003): one GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{defaultBranchSha}?recursive=1 call filtered on /^keyvault\d*$/i / keyvault.hcl under a root table (infrastructure/, azureDatabricks/), positional-agnostic appName/environment/qualifier derivation with a grouping-dir skip-list (keyvaults, _idmapplications), widened environment-agnostic shared heuristic /(^_?common$|^shared$)/i, delegates vaultName reconstruction to terragruntLocalsResolver.resolveName(vaultDir, target); returns { found, vaults: [{ vaultDir, vaultName, resourceGroup }], qualifiers? }, never assumes a single vault and surfaces the sub-app list when more than one resolves for (appName, environment). listSecretNames(target, appName, environment, vaultDir?) aggregates secrets.enc.yaml keys across all resolved vaults (or one, when vaultDir is supplied). submitSecretViaGitOps(target, appName, environment, vaultDir, secretName, encryptedValue, userEmail, correlationId) allow-list validates vaultDir against the current resolveKeyVaults() result BEFORE any path construction (an unvalidated client-supplied vaultDir would be an arbitrary-repo-path write), then commits to {vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml. Wraps githubService.getFileContent/createOrUpdateFile/createPullRequest and githubService.branchExists/findOpenPullRequest helpers. resolveKeyVaults caches the in-flight Promise (not the resolved value) in a Map keyed by `${target}` ALONE — repo-level, since one tree fetch answers every app/environment/vault lookup in that repo (re-scoped from the per-tuple key to satisfy the amended NFR-SCALE-001; the Round 1 B2 in-flight-Promise mechanism itself is preserved unchanged). submitSecretViaGitOps still never encrypts/decrypts the outer secrets.enc.yaml document itself — see technical.data_contracts.secrets_enc_yaml_format (Round 1 B1, preserved) — it SOPS-encrypts only the single value being submitted into a self-contained blob, then reads the outer YAML as plaintext, sets/replaces exactly one key, and writes it back. Before creating a branch it calls githubService.branchExists(repo, branchName); if true, it commits directly to that branch's current HEAD instead of calling createBranch (Round 1 B3, preserved). Branch name now includes vaultSlug (final segment of vaultDir) so two sibling vaults submitting the same secret name never collide on one branch.

NEW component (resolves Round 3 Blocking B3) — owns best-effort reconstruction of a vault's keyvaultname, which hclParser.js cannot do: hclParser.js only extracts module{}.source/version from a single file with zero cross-file locals resolution, expression evaluation, or comment stripping. resolveName(vaultDir, target): (1) fetches the target terragrunt.hcl plus common.hcl/env.hcl walking up parent folders (mirroring Terragrunt find_in_parent_folders() semantics), (2) parses each file's locals{} block and records which local name is bound to which read_terragrunt_config(find_in_parent_folders("X.hcl")) call, so local.<alias>.locals.keyvaultname resolves regardless of whether an app calls that alias env, config, or common_vars, (3) evaluates the small observed expression grammar — substr(s,start,len), format(...), "${a}-${b}" interpolation — not full HCL/Terraform expression evaluation, (4) strips full-line #/// comments before any assignment match so a commented-out '# keyvaultname = ...' line (confirmed in commHub/*/env.hcl) is never matched as live, and (5) only reads inputs.keyvaultname inside the matched keyvault*/terragrunt.hcl, ignoring any *_key_vault_name local encountered while resolving (Round 3 Advisory A2). Returns null (never throws) when the expression is unresolvable. Reuses the same githubService.octokit client and GitHub App auth as hclParser.js — not a new credential (Round 3 Advisory A3: git.getTree/git.getRef are standard REST calls under the existing Infrastructure GitHub App installation, no new permission required).

Add branchExists(repo, branchName) — thin wrapper over git.getRef('heads/{branchName}') returning true/false (catches 404, rethrows other errors), used so submitSecretViaGitOps can decide reuse-branch vs createBranch without createBranch throwing on an already-existing ref (resolves Round 1 Blocking B3). Add findOpenPullRequest(repo, branchName) using octokit.rest.pulls.list({ head: `${owner}:${branchName}`, state: 'open' }) — the `head` filter requires the `owner:` prefix, not a bare branch name (resolves Round 1 Advisory A2). Both mirror the existing pulls.list usage pattern already in this file. No changes to existing methods or auth clients.

Add GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment (accepts optional vaultDir and optional qualifier query params) and POST /api/secrets (accepts optional/required vaultDir and optional/required qualifier body fields per FR-002(l)), both requireAuth + express-validator with widened regexes appName /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, environment /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}$/, qualifier /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$/, following the app-metadata/feedback route conventions (logMetric on request/success/failure, correlationId in every response, no internal error leakage). Both handlers return HTTP 422 with the FR-003 vaults list when vaultDir is ambiguous or does not match, and with the FR-003 qualifiers list when qualifier is ambiguous or does not match, so the client can render a selector without a second round trip.
Add config.sops = { keyVaultUrl: process.env.SOPS_KEYVAULT_URL || '', keyName: process.env.SOPS_KEY_NAME || 'sops-master-key' } — read-only config, no secret material.
Add "secrets": false to every environment's features object.
Add secrets: boolean to EnvironmentConfig['features'] and to both fallback default env objects; add secretsEnabledEnvironments computed mirroring aksEnabledEnvironments.

Add getSecrets(appName, environment, target, qualifier?, vaultDir?) -> GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment?target=...&qualifier=...&vaultDir=... and submitSecret(payload) -> POST /api/secrets, payload including an optional/required vaultDir and an optional/required qualifier field per FR-002(l).

Target selector, app/environment selector (reuses GET /api/installed-apps), secrets list table (name, vaultDir/vaultName, lastUpdated), New Secret form, StatusModal.vue reused for a synchronous in-flight/terminal indicator (no useWorkflowPolling). Renders a required vault selector (populated from the FR-003 vaults list) whenever more than one vault resolves for the selected app/environment — submit stays disabled until a vault is chosen; the selector is hidden and that vault used implicitly when exactly one resolves. The secrets list offers a per-vault filter under the same condition so identically-named secrets in sibling vaults remain distinguishable.
Add { id: 'secrets', label: 'Secrets', requiresAuth: true } to allNavItems, same pattern as the existing feedback entry.

Import SecretsPage.vue; add a home-page card (gated by environmentsStore.secretsEnabledEnvironments.length > 0) and the currentPage === 'secrets' render branch, mirroring the existing FeedbackPage wiring.
Install the sops CLI binary in the runtime image stage (pinned version) so services/secretsService.js can shell out to it (resolves Round 1 Advisory A1). SRE DevOps phase action item.

flows.name: Happy path: create a new secret (single vault)
steps: Developer opens Secrets page, selects target (live/sand)
GET /api/installed-apps populates app/environment selector
GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment?target= resolves vaults via FR-003 (tree enumeration) and lists existing secret names; exactly one vault resolves, so no selector is shown
Developer clicks New Secret, enters name + value
POST /api/secrets validates input; vaultDir omitted and defaults to the single resolved vault

Backend allow-list validates vaultDir against FR-003's current result, SOPS-encrypts value, creates/updates branch secrets/{appName}-{environment}-{vaultSlug}-{secretName}, commits {vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml, opens PR
Response { success, correlationId, prNumber, prUrl } returned synchronously; StatusModal shows terminal success with PR link
Platform engineer reviews/merges PR (human-timed, unbounded, not tracked by portal)
Developer's next GET /api/secrets call reflects the merged secret

flows.name: Multiple vaults resolved: disambiguation required
steps: FR-003 resolves more than one vault for the app/environment (e.g. mlops-style keyvault01+keyvault02)
GET /api/secrets aggregates secrets across all resolved vaults, each entry tagged with its vaultDir; SecretsPage.vue shows a per-vault filter
Developer opens New Secret form; a required vault selector renders from the vaults list, submit disabled until one is chosen

POST /api/secrets without vaultDir -> 422 { error, vaults, correlationId }; with a vaultDir that doesn't match FR-003's list -> 422; with a matching vaultDir -> proceeds, commits to that vault's secrets.enc.yaml only

flows.name: Concurrent submission conflict (same vault)
steps: Two developers submit different secrets for the same app/environment/target/vaultDir close together
Second submission's pre-PR SHA check finds that vaultDir's secrets.enc.yaml SHA changed since branch creation
Backend aborts without merge attempt, returns 503 { error: 'Concurrent secret submission, please retry', correlationId }
Developer resubmits; a fresh commit/branch/PR is opened based on the new HEAD

flows.name: Concurrent submissions to sibling vaults (no conflict)
steps: Two developers submit secrets for the same app/environment but different vaultDir values (e.g. keyvault01 vs keyvault02)
Each submission's SHA check reads its own vaultDir's secrets.enc.yaml, which the other submission never touches
Both submissions succeed independently; neither triggers the 503 conflict path

flows.name: Duplicate open PR (idempotency)
steps: Developer submits the same secretName twice within a short window for the same vaultDir
Backend finds an existing open PR on branch secrets/{appName}-{environment}-{vaultSlug}-{secretName}
Returns 409 { error: 'A PR for this secret is already open', prUrl, correlationId }

error_scenarios.scenario: No qualifying vault directory/file found (FR-003 found=false)
Multiple vaults resolved and vaultDir omitted/ambiguous
error_scenarios.handling: FR-001 vaultDir filter mismatch -> 422; FR-002 vaultDir omitted or not an allow-listed match -> 422 with vaults list

error_scenarios.scenario: Duplicate open PR for same branch
error_scenarios.handling: No new branch/commit; return existing PR URL

error_scenarios.scenario: Concurrent secrets.enc.yaml mutation on the same vaultDir (SHA mismatch)
error_scenarios.handling: Abort, no merge attempt, ask caller to retry; a sibling vaultDir's concurrent write is unaffected
Catch child_process error, log correlationId only (no value), return generic message
Catch, structured error, never throw raw stack to client
Fall back to per-directory listing for the requested appName; log warn with correlationId; never silently return found:false
resolveKeyVaults returns { found:false, vaults:[] }; route returns 404 not 500

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets happy path (single vault, vaultDir omitted) returns prNumber/prUrl and never logs secretValue
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 200 response shape matches contract; log spy asserts no 'value' key logged

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets with resolveKeyVaults found=false returns 422
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 422 { success:false }

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets with found=true, vaultName=null proceeds (not an error); commit path derives from vaultDir, not vaultName
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 200 success, not 422

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets when FR-003 resolves multiple vaults and vaultDir is omitted returns 422 with the vaults list
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 422 { success:false, error, vaults }

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets when FR-003 resolves multiple vaults and the supplied vaultDir does not exactly match one of them returns 422 (allow-list rejection); no path is constructed
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 422 { success:false }; githubService.createOrUpdateFile never called

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets when FR-003 resolves multiple vaults and a valid vaultDir is supplied commits to {vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml and opens a branch whose name includes vaultSlug
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 200 success; commit path and branch name both derive from the supplied vaultDir

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets duplicate open PR on same branch (same appName-environment-vaultSlug-secretName) returns 409 with prUrl
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 409 { prUrl }

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets SHA mismatch on the same vaultDir's secrets.enc.yaml (concurrent edit) returns 503, no merge attempted
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 503 { success:false }; githubService merge/rebase never called

functional_test_scenarios.description: Concurrent POST /api/secrets to two DIFFERENT sibling vaultDir values of the same app/environment both succeed; neither triggers the 503 conflict path
functional_test_scenarios.expected: both requests return 200; each vaultDir's SHA check only ever compares against its own file

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults resolves a single vault with a reconstructable name (canonical depth-2 layout)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: { found:true, vaults: [{ vaultDir, vaultName: <string>, resourceGroup }] }, vaults.length === 1

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults resolves numbered vault directories keyvault01 + keyvault02 in one environment (mlops-style) as two distinct vaults
functional_test_scenarios.expected: vaults.length === 2, distinct vaultDir values

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults correctly derives appName/environment for a depth-3 environment layout ({app}/hub/{env}, doccafe-style)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found:true, vaultDir/appName/environment match the depth-3 path, not misparsed as depth-2

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults correctly derives appName/environment for sub-app nesting ({app}/{env}/{subapp}, linuxVms/acunetix-style) without treating the sub-app segment as the environment
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found:true, environment matches the requested value, not the subapp segment

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults matches Key Vault config expressed as a file rather than a directory (infrastructure/itg/_common/keyvault.hcl)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found:true, vaultDir points at the containing directory for the matched file

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults ignores a commented-out '# keyvaultname = ...' line in env.hcl in favor of the live assignment below it (commHub-style)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: vaultName reflects only the live (uncommented) assignment

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults returns found=false when no qualifying vault directory/file exists
functional_test_scenarios.expected: { found:false, vaults: [] }

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults falls back to per-directory listing for the requested appName when the trees API response returns truncated:true, logging a warn with the correlation ID instead of silently returning found:false
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found reflects the fallback listing's result; a warn-level log line with correlationId is emitted

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults repo-level cache: 10 concurrent calls across DIFFERING app/environment tuples for the same target trigger exactly 1 underlying GitHub trees API call (in-flight Promise keyed by target alone)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: underlying githubService tree-fetch call is made exactly once even when all 10 calls (for different appName/environment combinations) fire before the first resolves

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults returns found=false/vaults=[] and logs a warning (does not throw) when the target repo is unconfigured
functional_test_scenarios.expected: { found:false, vaults:[] }; no exception propagates

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveName follows local.<alias>.locals.keyvaultname indirection into env.hcl under each observed alias (env, config, common_vars) — parameterized
functional_test_scenarios.expected: all three alias variants resolve to the correct keyvaultname value

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveName evaluates substr()-based and separator-less concatenation/interpolation expressions with per-app length/format variance
functional_test_scenarios.expected: each observed expression form (substr(local.prefix,0,N)-…, ${local.prefix}${local.envName}app-kv-1, partially-hardcoded, fully literal) resolves to the expected string

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveName returns null (does not throw) when an expression is genuinely unresolvable
functional_test_scenarios.expected: null returned; caller (resolveKeyVaults) still reports found:true for that vaultDir

functional_test_scenarios.description: Secrets page renders target selector and list without value fields
functional_test_scenarios.expected: no element/text renders a raw secret value

functional_test_scenarios.description: Submitting the form calls POST /api/secrets and shows terminal success with PR link (no polling)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: useWorkflowPolling composable is not invoked

functional_test_scenarios.description: Vault selector renders and is required when the list call resolves more than one vault; submit stays disabled until a vault is chosen; selector is hidden when exactly one vault resolves
functional_test_scenarios.expected: submit button disabled state toggles correctly on vault selection; selector absent for the single-vault case

functional_test_scenarios.description: secretsEnabledEnvironments filters to only enabled+secrets:true environments
functional_test_scenarios.expected: matches aksEnabledEnvironments filter semantics

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults resolves vaults under BOTH roots in a single tree enumeration: a path like azureDatabricks/itg/keyvault is found alongside infrastructure/mlops/dev/keyvault01 in the same call
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found:true, vaults includes azureDatabricks/itg/keyvault with synthetic appName='azureDatabricks'; the previous parts[0] !== 'infrastructure' guard does not drop azureDatabricks paths

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults matches infrastructure/ayaApplications/ayaCoreServices/keyvaults/shared/keyvault as environment-agnostic — a request for environment='dev' (or any non-shared env) still resolves this shared vault
functional_test_scenarios.expected: found:true, the shared vault appears in vaults for every requested environment (widened heuristic /(^_?common$|^shared$)/i)

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults treats infrastructure/idm/_idmapplications/notif/dev/keyvault and infrastructure/idm/_idmapplications/autobk/dev/keyvault as DISTINCT sub-apps under appName='idm', environment='dev' — qualifier is 'notif' for the first and 'autobk' for the second; grouping dir '_idmapplications' is skipped, not treated as the environment
functional_test_scenarios.expected: qualifiers list is ['autobk','notif']; each individual resolveKeyVaults('idm','dev','live','notif') returns the notif vault only

functional_test_scenarios.description: resolveKeyVaults for idm/dev WITHOUT a qualifier returns qualifiers:['autobk','notif'] so the client can render a sub-app selector; resolution still does not assume a single vault and does not silently pick one
functional_test_scenarios.expected: { found:true, vaults: [], qualifiers:['autobk','notif'] } when (idm, dev) resolves >1 sub-apps and qualifier is omitted

functional_test_scenarios.description: express-validator accepts the widened appName (azureDatabricks, facilityContracts — up to 64 chars), environment (shared-services with hyphen — up to 32 chars), and qualifier (notif — up to 64 chars) regexes; rejects values still over those bounds
functional_test_scenarios.expected: previously-rejected real-tree values now validate; over-bound values still 400

functional_test_scenarios.description: POST /api/secrets with qualifier='notif' when FR-003 resolves >1 sub-apps for (idm, dev) proceeds; with qualifier omitted and >1 sub-apps returns 422 { qualifiers:['autobk','notif'] }; with qualifier='fake' returns 422 (allow-list rejection)
functional_test_scenarios.expected: qualifier flows into the branch name as 'notif-' prefix and is reflected in the PR description; allow-list mismatches are rejected with the qualifiers list

functional_test_scenarios.description: GET /api/secrets/azureDatabricks/itg?target=live returns 200 with vaultDir='azureDatabricks/itg/keyvault' (FR-003 azureDatabricks root); same call against target=sand is out of scope and returns 404
functional_test_scenarios.expected: azureDatabricks paths are reachable via a single synthetic app selector entry, not silently dropped

functional_test_scenarios.description: GET /api/secrets/ayaApplications/ayaCoreServices/dev?target=live resolves infrastructure/ayaApplications/ayaCoreServices/keyvaults/shared/keyvault for environment='dev' because of the widened shared heuristic
functional_test_scenarios.expected: 200, vaultDir includes the shared keyvault; previously this returned 404 when environment != 'shared'

functional_test_scenarios.description: When FR-003 returns qualifiers.length > 1 for the selected (appName, environment), the page renders a required sub-app selector and submit stays disabled until a qualifier is chosen; when qualifiers.length === 1 the selector is hidden and the qualifier is implicit
functional_test_scenarios.expected: submit button disabled state toggles correctly on qualifier selection; selector absent for the single-sub-app case

e2e_test_scenarios.description: Full create-secret flow with secrets feature flag enabled in devsand, single-vault app
steps: Navigate to Secrets page
Select target=sand, an app, an environment
Assert existing secrets list renders without values
Open New Secret form, submit a name+value
Assert terminal success state shows a PR link

e2e_test_scenarios.description: Multi-vault app requires explicit vault selection before submit is enabled
steps: Navigate to Secrets page, select target=live and a multi-vault app/environment
Assert the secrets list shows entries from more than one vault with a per-vault filter
Open New Secret form; assert submit is disabled until a vault is selected
Select a vault, submit a name+value
Assert terminal success state shows a PR link and the PR targets the selected vault's directory

e2e_test_scenarios.description: azureDatabricks root surfaces as a synthetic appName in the secrets page; selection resolves to azureDatabricks/<env>/keyvault paths
steps: Navigate to Secrets page, select target=live
Assert the app selector includes 'azureDatabricks' as a selectable entry
Select azureDatabricks and an environment (e.g. itg)
Assert the secrets list renders for azureDatabricks/<env>/keyvault (Round 4 widening — previously this app/environment returned 404)

e2e_test_scenarios.description: Sub-app selector surfaces when (appName, environment) resolves >1 qualifiers (e.g. idm with multiple _idmapplications sub-apps)
steps: Navigate to Secrets page, select target=live, appName='idm', environment='dev'
Assert a required sub-app selector appears with the distinct sub-app names (e.g. autobk, notif)
Assert submit is disabled until a sub-app is chosen
Select a sub-app, submit a name+value
Assert terminal success state shows a PR link whose branch name includes the qualifier prefix

nfrs.target: p95 latency <= 2000ms on both secrets endpoints

nfrs.verification: CI grep scan for 'secretValue' logged key + SOPS-decrypt check on committed files

nfrs.target: Portal SP has wrapKey-only on sops-master-key, no per-app vault role
100% of new handlers use validationResult guard before I/O
Duplicate submission -> 409 with existing PR URL, no dup PR
10 concurrent requests across DIFFERING app/environment tuples for the same target -> 1 GitHub tree API call per replica (repo-level cache key, 5 min TTL, in-flight Promise shared across tuples)
Every endpoint emits logMetric with correlationId/user/target/appName/environment/latency_ms on success and failure paths
SecretsPage.vue reuses StatusModal.vue synchronously, no custom modal/polling
Feature hidden unless features.secrets=true for the environment; default false everywhere

external_tools: sops CLI binary must be present in the runtime container image (Dockerfile — see component_changes), invoked via child_process with the azure_keyvault creation rule
